title: Research: Embedded vendor BIOS scraping feasibility (DFI, Advantech, IBASE, Sapphire, etc.)
description:
Question: 

Context: 

Findings: 

Question: Is automated scraping of AMD Ryzen Embedded / EPYC Embedded board BIOSes feasible from any public source?

Context:
- BOARD_CLASSES tuple in src/psp_etl/ingest.py reserves an 'Embedded' value, but no scraper currently populates it. Only manual ROM ingest can set it today.
- Embedded boards run AMD Ryzen Embedded (V1000/V2000/V3000, R1000/R2000) and EPYC Embedded (3000, 7000, 8004, 9004) parts — different microarchitecture lineage from consumer/server, often interesting from a PSP-firmware-divergence perspective.

Vendors to investigate:
- DFI (https://www.dfi.com/) — large embedded-board catalog, AMD lineup includes COM-HPC modules and SBCs.
- Advantech (https://www.advantech.com/) — login-required for many BIOSes.
- IBASE (https://www.ibase.com.tw/) — AMD V-series industrial boards.
- SECO (https://www.seco.com/) — Embedded systems integrator.
- Sapphire (https://www.sapphiretech.com/) — IPC product line includes AMD EDGE-series.
- Compulab (https://www.compulab.com/) — Fitlet / Airtop AMD systems.
- Mini-ITX vendor pages (Asrock Rack actually counts here too — IMB-X1715 etc.).

What to capture:
- For each vendor: does the support portal require login? Is the BIOS download exposed via a stable URL? Are there CDN paths archived in Wayback?
- Many embedded vendors use an authenticated 'partner portal' — those are out-of-scope.
- Some vendors bundle BIOS into a 'BSP' tarball that also contains drivers; unwrapping is feasible but needs per-vendor format knowledge.

Outcome:
- A short comparison table (similar to #79's prior-art survey) capturing: portal type, auth requirement, archive coverage, BIOS package format, recommended access strategy or 'unsupported'.
- File per-vendor follow-up scraper issues for the vendors where automated scraping is viable.
- For vendors where it isn't viable, document in README as 'manual ingest only' and close.

This issue produces follow-up work, not code directly.

Related: #79.
